newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end mixed on NCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end mixed on NCD issue.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed mixed on Wednesday following the central bank's issue of T$10 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess money, dealers said.
Liquidity remained relatively loose due to the arrival of the peak monthly period for money returning to the banking system following early-month outflows, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.908 percent against Tuesday's 5.968 close, still outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone, with 30-day commercial paper at 6.00 percent against 5.90-6.00.
Wednesday's NCD issue, the fifth in five days, was the highest in value since the central bank began its current round of issues on March 3.
Dealers said they expected short-term rates to remain stable or slightly higher in the near term on the central bank moves.

In an apparent strategy to stave off overheating in the red-hot stock market, central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Monday the bank would continue to issue NCDs to mop up banking system liquidity.
Government bond yields fell on short-covering triggered by the day's stock market correction, with the 10-year 86/4 bond yield at 6.1400-1425 percent against 6.1450.
Taiwan share prices suffered their first loss on Wednesday following seven straight days of gains, ending down 84.68 points or 0.99 percent at 8,441.52.
